facts.statement: A Unenlagia skeleton was discovered in the Sierra del Portezuelo in Neuquén province, Argentina, in 1996.
facts.quote: In 1996 in the Neuquén province of Argentina a skeleton of a theropod was discovered in the Sierra del Portezuelo and reported the same year.

facts.statement: Fernando Novas and Pablo Puerta named and described the species Unenlagia comahuensis in 1997.
facts.quote: In 1997 Fernando Emilio Novas and Pablo Puerta named and described Unenlagia comahuensis.

facts.statement: The name Unenlagia means 'half-bird' in Mapudungun, reflecting the describers' view of it as a link between birds and basal theropods.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Mapuche uñùm, 'bird', and llag, 'half', in reference to the fact that the describers considered the species to be a link between birds and more basal theropods.

facts.statement: A second species, Unenlagia paynemili, was named and described in 2004 based on a skeleton found near Lago Barreales in 2002.
facts.quote: In 2002 near the Lago Barreales a second skeleton was uncovered and reported in 2003. In 2004 it was named and described by Jorge Calvo, Juan Porfiri and Alexander Kellner as a second species: Unenlagia paynemili.

facts.statement: Unenlagia lived in Argentina approximately 90 million years ago.
facts.quote: Habitó en Argentina hace alrededor de 90 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype of Unenlagia comahuensis is a partial skeleton from the Coniacian age that lacks a skull but includes vertebrae, ribs, a scapula, and leg bones.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MCF PVPH 78, was uncovered in layers of the Portezuelo Formation dating to the Coniacian. It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull but including vertebrae, a sacrum, ribs, chevrons, a scapula, a humerus, a partial pelvis, a femur and a tibia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Unenlagia paynemili consists of a humerus and two pubic bones.
facts.quote: The holotype is MUCPv-349, a partial skeleton consisting of a humerus and two pubes.

facts.statement: Research suggests the scapula of Unenlagia was likely located on the side of the ribcage rather than flat on top, similar to other theropods.
facts.quote: However, in 2002 Kenneth Carpenter pointed out that this would imply that the shoulder-blade was dorsoventrally flattened instead of laterally as with other theropods and that it thus were more likely the scapula was located on the side of the ribcage.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that non-avian theropods like Unenlagia could not lift their forelimbs above their backs.
facts.quote: This conformed to a later hypothesis by Philip Senter that non-avian theropods like Unenlagia were unable to lift their forelimbs above their back, as even would still have been the case for the basalmost bird Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: South American researchers argue that a laterally positioned scapula would cause the coracoid to protrude into the ribcage, which they find anatomically implausible.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los trabajadores sudamericanos no han quedado convencidos, respondiendo que una escápula colocada lateralmente haría que la coracoides de Unenlagia sobresaliera en su caja torácica, lo que parece anatómicamente inverosímil.

facts.statement: Estimates of Unenlagia's size vary, with some suggesting a length of 3.5 meters and weight of 75 kg, while others suggest a length of just 2 meters.
facts.quote: Estimates have thus varied between a length of 3.5 m and a weight of 75 kg on the one hand, and a length of just 2 m on the other.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated Unenlagia to be 2.3 meters long and weigh between 9.1 and 22.7 kilograms.
facts.quote: However, Thomas Holtz has estimated Unenlagia at 2.3 m long and 9.1-22.7 kg (20-50 lbs) in weight.

facts.statement: In its original description, Unenlagia was considered a basal member of the Avialae, making it a sister taxon to birds.
facts.quote: Novas and Puerta in the original description considered Unenlagia a sister taxon of the birds, which would make it a basal member of the Avialae sensu Gauthier 1986.

facts.statement: Mark Norell and Peter Makovicky classified Unenlagia as a member of the Dromaeosauridae in 1999.
facts.quote: However, in 1999 Mark Norell and Peter Makovicky stated that Unenlagia was a member of the Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: Unenlagia belongs to the bird-like dromaeosaurid subfamily Unenlagiinae and is closely related to Buitreraptor and Neuquenraptor.
facts.quote: Unenlagia would have belonged to the extremely bird-like Gondwanan clade of dromaeosaurids called the Unenlagiinae, and be closely related to species such as Buitreraptor and Neuquenraptor (which might be the same species as Unenlagia).

facts.statement: The classification of Unenlagiinae is debated, with some studies placing the group within Avialae rather than Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: This position has not been unanimously accepted. In 2011 Novas and Federico Agnolín published a study in which a Unenlagiidae was positioned within Avialae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Unenlagia evolved from flying ancestors and became flightless, or if bird-like flight evolved independently multiple times.
facts.quote: Makovicky et al. in 2005 also recovered the 'flying raptor' Rahonavis as a member of this group, which would mean that either Unenlagia is secondarily flightless, having evolved from flying, Rahonavis-like ancestors, or that bird-like flight evolved at least twice.

facts.statement: Unenlagia is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Unenlagia belongs to the subfamily Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Unenlagiinae

facts.statement: The first skeleton of Unenlagia was discovered in 1996 in the Sierra del Portezuelo, Neuquén province, Argentina.
facts.quote: En 1996 en la provincia de Neuquén de Argentina se descubrió un esqueleto de un terópodo en la Sierra del Portezuelo y se reportó el mismo año.

facts.statement: Fernando Emilio Novas and Pablo Puerta named and described the species Unenlagia comahuensis in 1997.
facts.quote: En 1997 Fernando Emilio Novas y Pablo Puerta nombraron y describieron Unenlagia comahuensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Unenlagia combines the Mapuche words for 'bird' and 'half', reflecting the describers' view of it as a link between birds and basal theropods.
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva del mapuche uñùm, pájaro, y llag, mitad, en referencia a que los descriptores consideraban a la especie como un nexo entre las aves y los terópodos más basales.

facts.statement: The species name comahuensis refers to the Comahue region where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie hace referencia al Comahue, región donde se realizó el hallazgo.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MCF PVPH 78 was found in Coniacian-aged layers of the Portezuelo Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MCF PVPH 78, fue descubierto en capas de la Formación Portezuelo que datan del Coniaciense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull but including vertebrae, a sacrum, ribs, chevrons, a scapula, a humerus, a partial pelvis, a femur, and a tibia.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial sin cráneo pero que incluye vértebras, un sacro, costillas, cheurones, una escápula, un húmero, una pelvis parcial, un fémur y una tibia.

facts.statement: A second skeleton was discovered near Lago Barreales in 2002 and reported in 2003.
facts.quote: En 2002 cerca del Lago Barreales se descubrió un segundo esqueleto y se reportó en 2003.

facts.statement: Jorge Calvo, Juan Porfiri, and Alexander Kellner named and described the second species, Unenlagia paynemili, in 2004.
facts.quote: En 2004 fue nombrado y descrito por Jorge Calvo , Juan Porfiri y Alexander Kellner como una segunda especie, Unenlagia paynemili.

facts.statement: The specific name paynemili honors Maximino Paynemil, the chief of the Paynemil community.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Maximino Paynemil, el jefe de la comunidad Paynemil.

facts.statement: The holotype for U. paynemili is specimen MUCPv-349, a partial skeleton consisting of a humerus and two pubic bones.
facts.quote: El holotipo es MUCPv-349, un esqueleto parcial que consta de un húmero y dos pubis.

facts.statement: Some researchers consider Neuquenraptor to be a subjective junior synonym of Unenlagia.
facts.quote: Algunos investigadores consideran que Neuquenraptor es un sinónimo subjetivo menor de Unenlagia.

facts.statement: In their original description, Novas and Puerta considered Unenlagia to be the sister taxon of birds, making it a basal member of Avialae.
facts.quote: Novas y Puerta en la descripción original consideraban a Unenlagia un taxón hermano de las aves, lo que lo convertiría en un miembro basal de Avialae sensu Gauthier 1986.

facts.statement: In 1999, Mark Norell and Peter Makovicky argued that Unenlagia belonged to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1999 Mark Norell y Peter Makovicky afirmaron que Unenlagia era miembro de Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: The classification of Unenlagia within Dromaeosauridae has not been accepted unanimously by the scientific community.
facts.quote: Esta posición no ha sido aceptada por unanimidad.

facts.statement: In 2011, Novas and Federico Agnolín published a study placing the family Unenlagiidae within Avialae.
facts.quote: En 2011 Novas y Federico Agnolín publicaron un estudio en el que se posicionaba un Unenlagiidae dentro de Avialae.

facts.statement: A 2019 cladogram by Hartman et al. places Unenlagia as a more derived member alongside Dakotaraptor.
facts.quote: A continuación se muestra un cladograma realizado por Hartman et al. 2019, en el que se encuentra que Unenlagia es un miembro más derivado junto con Dakotaraptor.

facts.statement: A 2020 cladogram by Motta et al. shows that Unenlagia is more derived than traditional dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Este cladograma es de Motta et al., 2020, que muestra que Unenlagia es más derivado que los dromeosáuridos tradicionales.

facts.statement: Unenlagia lived during the Coniacian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, MCF PVPH 78, fue descubierto en capas de la Formación Portezuelo que datan del Coniaciense.

facts.statement: The genus Unenlagia existed from the Turonian to the Coniacian, approximately 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database classifies Unenlagia within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Unenlagia is placed in the subfamily Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Unenlagiinae
